title: Wire the FSD layer rules into the frontend app

frontend.description: Target frontend — decides the layer set the guide prints. Next.js has no FSD 'app' layer (its App Router directory is it) and its pages layer is the _pages/ directory (FSD's Next.js guide: Next.js reads src/pages as its Pages Router). Omitted: toolkit.config.json's frontend (init records it); required when none is recorded

project.description: The frontend app whose eslint.config.mjs gets the rule and whose source root holds the layers. Omitted: the workspace's one frontend application (e2e projects and the backend api are not candidates); with more than one, the run is refused with the candidates listed

enforcement.description: Severity of the archweave/fsd-boundaries ESLint rule. The rule is canonical FSD either way; only how hard it reports differs (Team preset: error; Solo / Quick Start: warn). Defaults to toolkit.config.json's fsd.enforcement, else warn

applyEslint.description: Write the rule into the app's ESLint config instead of printing a paste-ready snippet. The create CLI passes this on workspaces it just created; leave it off to keep an existing config untouched

steiger.description: Also set up steiger, the official FSD linter, as an opt-in fsd-check target: writes the app's steiger.config.mjs (recommended rules; an existing config is kept), adds the target to the app and the two devDependencies to the root package.json, and prints the install command. Needs Node >= 22.18

locale.description: Report and snippet language. Defaults to toolkit.config.json's locale, else en

dryRun.description: Print the report (including what --applyEslint would write) without writing anything
